package_info.why_malicious: FurBall is a surveillance malware distributed as a trojanized Android application, masquerading as the official app for the Teheran restaurant 'Mohsen'. It is operated by the Domestic Kitten APT group to target Iranian expats and dissidents. The malware abuses Android permissions to collect and exfiltrate sensitive user data—including contacts, location, microphone, camera, SMS, and call logs—to attacker-controlled infrastructure, enabling persistent surveillance and privacy violations.

execution_context.trigger: after installation and on app launch
execution_context.file_location: main application code (AndroidManifest.xml and core Java classes within APK)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Upon installation, the application requests permissions for contacts, location, microphone, camera, SMS, call logs, and storage. Once granted, the app periodically collects data from these sources and uploads the information to a remote command-and-control server via background network requests.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime after installation, the code requests and leverages broad Android permissions to access contacts, location, microphone, camera, SMS, and call logs, then periodically collects this data and transmits it via HTTP(S) POST requests to a hardcoded remote command-and-control server, resulting in covert exfiltration of sensitive user information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The application requests a wide range of sensitive permissions that are unnecessary for a restaurant app, and it collects and uploads private user data to an external server without user awareness or consent. The background exfiltration of data is indicative of spyware activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate restaurant app would only require minimal permissions (such as internet access for menu updates or location for finding nearby branches) and would never access or transmit contacts, SMS, call logs, microphone, or camera data. The observed behavior is a clear violation of user privacy and platform guidelines.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Device management or parental control apps may request similar permissions, but they do so with explicit user consent, clear disclosure, and visible user controls. Such apps are also typically distributed through official app stores with transparent privacy policies.
key_indicators: Requests for sensitive permissions (contacts, SMS, call logs, microphone, camera) unrelated to restaurant functionality
Background services that periodically collect and transmit user data
Hardcoded remote server endpoints for data exfiltration
Masquerading as a legitimate local service to gain user trust
Absence of user-facing features corresponding to the permissions requested

attack_chain.action: User is deceived into downloading and installing the FurBall APK, believing it to be the official app for the Teheran restaurant 'Mohsen'.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware is installed on the device and requests excessive permissions.

attack_chain.action: Upon launch, the app requests and is granted permissions to access sensitive data sources including contacts, location, microphone, camera, SMS, and call logs.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware gains access to sensitive user data.

attack_chain.action: The malware periodically collects data from the granted sources and prepares it for exfiltration.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive data is staged for transmission to the attacker.

attack_chain.action: Collected data is transmitted via background network requests to a hardcoded remote command-and-control server controlled by the attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives exfiltrated sensitive information, enabling ongoing surveillance.

behavioral_signatures: Android applications requesting multiple sensitive permissions (contacts, SMS, call logs, microphone, camera) without clear justification
Background services or scheduled tasks that collect and transmit user data without user interaction
Network traffic from non-communication apps to hardcoded or suspicious remote servers
Apps masquerading as local services (e.g., restaurant apps) with hidden surveillance functionality
file_indicators: APK files with package names or app names mimicking legitimate local services but containing code for background data collection
AndroidManifest.xml files declaring excessive permissions unrelated to stated app purpose
Presence of hardcoded C2 server URLs or IPs within the APK resources or code
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP(S) POST requests to attacker-controlled domains or IP addresses from restaurant-themed apps
Unusual periodic data uploads from apps that should not require background network activity
Connections to infrastructure previously associated with Domestic Kitten APT operations
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Android applications that request sensitive permissions not aligned with their stated purpose, especially those distributed outside official app stores. Analyze network traffic for background connections to suspicious or hardcoded domains/IPs from non-communication apps. Use static and dynamic analysis to identify APKs with code for background data collection and exfiltration. Correlate app metadata (name, icon, package name) with known legitimate services to detect impersonation.
